a.text: Children of the wilds, where does your road lead?
Desert of blazing winds, how many have been lost in your sands?
Your final choice, is it where your heart truly points?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Good afternoon, sir!
The young Caprinae pants as she pushes open the glass door, stepping into the bar's gentle light.
The only other person in the establishment is a man behind the counter, startled by her entrance.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Oh, err, hey, miss.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Sorry, but we're not open yet.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Come back in the evening—

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: N-No, I'm not here for a drink.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Are you still hiring security?
The owner's eyes widen for a moment, but he soon walks out from behind the counter, stretching out a hand.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Oh, so that's what this was about. Well, come on then, have a seat.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Here, water.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Th-Thank you.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I saw the poster stuck to the board downstairs, and ran up as fast as I could.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: This place is... really nice. A proper downtown bar.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Whoops, I forgot to even ask your name.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: I'm Clarson, but just Clars will do.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I'm Hadiya Talun, sir.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Alright then, Miss Talun.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: You can put those, err... weapons aside. We're just talking for now.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Oh, sorry, the last few places I applied to wanted me to demonstrate my... Err...

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: My 'ability to respond to emergencies'.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: And I feel more confident with them around, so...

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Personally, what I look for most in a bouncer is professionalism.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: I'm not here to hire brawlers. I don't want you talking with your fists.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: You don't need to worry about that, Mr. Clars.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I'm not some hot-headed thug or anything. Look, these are my certificates.
Hadiya takes out a folder and passes it across the table to Clars, who is sitting on the sofa.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Huh. Never seen someone in this line of work come this prepared.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Let's see here...

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Training certifications... Weapon handling licenses...

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: This is pretty comprehensive. Some of my friends have combat training, but you hardly ever see a resume as spotless this one.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: To be frank, qualifications like these could get you into a legit security firm.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Not sure why you'd settle for being a bouncer.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I prefer more relaxed places like this, and I like this kind of work.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: (Quietly) Besides... the security firms never called back...

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Hmm? You say something?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Ah, nonono.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I was just saying the job market's not so great right now, even for security work.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I've visited a lot of places, but unfortunately none of them decided to hire me.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Well, that's weird.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Surely a resume like this would open a lot of doors?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: You'd think so, right? But the interviewers always said I wasn't tall enough, or intimidating enough.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Some of them even cut off the interview before we finished, for whatever reason.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Well, it's definitely not a problem with you, Miss Talun. They're the ones who wouldn't know talent if it bit 'em.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Whether it's your appearance or your experience, I've got no complaints at least.

spans.text: Whether it's your appearance or your experience,

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Now, with that out of the way, let's talk wages and hours. If they work for you, you can start as soon as tomorrow.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Really? Thank you, sir.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: This is the first time the hiring process had gone so smoothly. I'm glad I stuck it out for one more application.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Haha, means you found the right place.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Do you know how long it took to convince my folks to let me start a business, back in the day? People need to believe in themselves, and have the courage to take on new challenges.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: You're absolutely right. My family always hoped I'd carry on their mission with the same determination.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: To tell you the truth, I've struggled a lot with whether I should or not, but now that I've found what I want to do, things couldn't be better.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: That's exactly what I'm talking about!

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Okay, let's talk hours first. Your shift is from 8pm until 4am. I take it you have no objections to a graveyard shift?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: None at all, Mr. Clars!

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I was already following a similar schedule before I even applied.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: It wasn't formal work experience, but I'm used to it, so it won't be a problem.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Oh, helping out at the family store, that sort of thing?
Hadiya nods, and Clarson gives her a smile of satisfaction in return.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Great, you won't need much time to adjust. That simplifies things.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Where's the store you were helping out at, if you don't mind me asking?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: 57th Street.
The very second Hadiya mentions her neighborhood's name, thunder rumbles through the bar's window.
The cheerful smile on the bar owner's face freezes. It is as if he is suddenly unsure what expression he should be making. His mouth lies half-open as he stares awkwardly at Hadiya.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Mr. Clars?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Is... Is there a problem?
After a few seconds, Clarson finally seems to come to a decision. He puts down Hadiya's files and closes his eyes as he slowly shakes his head.
When he reopens them, his expression has turned grave.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: First, let's make sure I didn't mishear you, Miss Talun. You're from 57th Street?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I grew up there.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I haven't been looking for a job in this neighborhood for long, but I don't see how where I'm from should matter.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: But that's exactly the problem.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: You really have no idea why everyone you met here turned you down, do you?
The evening rain begins to fall outside as she replays today's experiences in her mind.

steps.name: Shrewd Bar Owner
steps.text: Our customers are rather fussy, Miss Talun. I'm afraid you're not going to give them a sense of security with the way you look.

steps.name: Shrewd Bar Owner
steps.text: And if our customers aren't satisfied, our business will suffer. Sorry, but you'll have to look elsewhere.

steps.name: Arrogant Bar Owner
steps.text: Not gonna mince words: we don't hire people like you.

steps.name: Arrogant Bar Owner
steps.text: You're tiny minus the horns, and 'tiny' ain't what we put in the job description. Go somewhere else.

steps.name: Greedy Bar Owner
steps.text: We don't have any openings at the moment, unless you're willing to do an unpaid trial period.

steps.name: Greedy Bar Owner
steps.text: I have too much to lose if I end up hiring the wrong sort of person, after all.

steps.name: Greedy Bar Owner
steps.text: Not happy with that? Then there's nothing to discuss. We don't take your kind here.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: No way...

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: But why?

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: I'm really sorry, Miss Talun, but I can't hire you either.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Let me give it to you straight:

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: You're not going to find any decent work around here with your background.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: That's ridiculous...

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Since long before the business district grew to what it is now, the locals have been feuding with immigrants over land and resources.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Even since the shops opened up, there've been quite a few incidents ending in bloodshed.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Most folks in this city just don't trust immigrants.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: And maybe you haven't noticed, but 57th street is where they all live.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: I'm sure your dad or granddad must've told you stories about the blood, sweat, and tears their generation put into building that neighborhood.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: But to us locals, that place represents nothing but grime and lawlessness.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I always thought life on the outside wouldn't be any different from 57th, just a small change in environment...

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Sounds like you grew up sheltered. Good on your family, honestly. But reality loves to disappoint.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Personally, I've got plenty of immigrant friends. I know they don't have it easy.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: But it is what it is. That's just... how this city operates.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: But we've lived here for decades...

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: It's not like we're fresh off the convoy!

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Yeah, and I didn't even notice a thing until you mentioned where you were from.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: But that won't change where you were born, and it won't change the prejudice my customers will have against you.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: I'm positive that's the only reason those other shops turned you away.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: (Is that why Luftar and the others left Columbia to become mercenaries?)

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: (Salma worked at that factory for less a month before being sent back. Was it for the same reason?)

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: (I always thought it was just bad luck...)

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I... never imagined it would be like this.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: And there you have it. But don't blame yourself—it's not your fault.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Here, take your things and go, quick.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: I'm sorry, but I can't help you any more than that. Besides—

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: It's just about opening hours.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Yeah. Sorry for bothering you, Mr. Clars.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Don't be. Just hurry on back home.

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: Take care. Looks like it's still raining.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Bar Owner
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Hadiya's Father
steps.text: I still hope you will return to Sargon one day, Hadiya.

steps.name: Hadiya's Father
steps.text: Do you remember the words passed down through our family? We are warriors of Sargon, descendants of the Qarnsayf.

steps.name: Hadiya's Father
steps.text: You must never forget the glorious history our ancestors wrote in the wilds, and their legends known to all.

steps.name: Hadiya's Father
steps.text: For one day our people will return to the wilds, and rebuild our tribe.

steps.name: Hadiya's Father
steps.text: It is a shame that our generation spent all our strength simply finding our footing in Columbia. None of us can return to Sargon.

steps.name: Hadiya's Father
steps.text: But yours still can. I believe you will be able to bring glory to our family.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: But we've been away from Sargon for too long, baba.

spans.text: But we've been away from Sargon for too long,

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: It's not that I don't want to, but it always feels too soon, like I'm not ready.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: It'd be amazing if I did manage to rebuild the tribe, but what exactly does that even mean?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Do I need a herd of burdenbeasts? Do I need a padishah worth swearing loyalty to? Or do I need to defeat the desert's strongest warriors?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I really have no idea where to even start. It might be best for me to stay in Columbia for now.

steps.name: Hadiya's Father
steps.text: Hadiya...

steps.name: Hadiya's Father
steps.text: I do not want to force you into doing anything, but...

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Relax, baba. Wherever I go, I won't disappoint you.

spans.text: . Wherever I go, I won't disappoint you.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Just have faith in your daughter, okay?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: (I thought this was going to be a chance for me to prove myself, but I never expected this.)

spans.text: (I thought this was going to be a chance for me to prove myself, but I never expected

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: (Should I look for work outside the city? No, there's no guarantee it'll be any better than here.)

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: (But where else can I even go? I can't just give up and go back home like this. That would be pathetic, after everything I said.)

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: (Whatever. I can't change what happened today, but I can come up with a new plan, starting tomorrow.)

spans.text: (Whatever. I can't change what happened today, but I
come up with a new plan, starting tomorrow.)

steps.text: Hadiya walks alone through the streets at night. All of a sudden, she feels ice-cold rainwater splash across her right leg.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Gah, what's a puddle doing there...? I didn't notice it at all...

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Ugh, why is it so hard for me to accept this? I already knew this wasn't going to be a walk in the park.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: But it's... It's just...!
Her hand cannot help but tighten its grip on her sword's hilt. She feels herself begin to shiver uncontrollably, and she knows it is not because of the chilly night.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: If only they'd give me a chance...

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I'd definitely—

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Hey, you there!

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Hands up! Drop the weapons!

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Wait! I didn't even do anything!

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Don't move! I said drop the weapons!

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Settle down, okay? I need these for work! I'm not doing anything bad with them!

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I have an open carry permit! There's no need to treat me like this!

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Cut the beastshit! Just put the weapons down, and no sudden movements! Don't make me use force!

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Hands on your head, and on your knees, facing the wall!

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: You deaf or something?! Follow my orders!

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Please don't do this, officer.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Look, I did as you said. I'm just on my way home, honest.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: That's what every criminal says. But what am I supposed to think when you're shuffling around at night with your head down, brandishing a sword?

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Name?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Hadiya bint Talun. Sir.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: A name like that... You Sargonian?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: No sir, I'm Columbian. I've lived on 57th Street my entire life.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I'm a full Columbian citizen.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I haven't broken any laws, officer. You can't just treat me like I'm guilty.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Yeah, that's not making you sound any more trustworthy.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: The Iron Hand Gang's been pretty active across the city lately. Most of their crew are Sargonian-Columbians, and they're holed up in 57th Street.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Someone with an innocent face like yours might be casing out joints for them.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Of course not. We've been law-abiding citizens for years. Why would we do that?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I've never even heard of this gang. Now can I—

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Don't move!

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Don't think you can talk your way out of this. What, you think 57th Street's got a squeaky-clean rep?

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: It's only common sense to treat you people with suspicion. Just because you live here doesn't give you the right to walk around like you own the place.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: This is slander, officer. I don't care what your reasons are; you can't just paint me with a brush like that—

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Shut it.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: I don't have time to argue with you. And I'm sure neither of us wants this to get ugly.
Hadiya feels the cold police-issue knife pressing against the back of her neck. She stares at the dirty brick wall and begins to shiver uncontrollably again.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: You got an ID? Where is it?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Inner jacket pocket. On the left.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Don't move a muscle. I'll get it.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: You'll be leaving here in an ambulance or worse if you try anything funny.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Well shit, there's your open carry permit. The hell is it even for, though? Your carefree days in that shitty block of yours not enough for you?

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Sheesh, and that's some spotless paperwork on you. Got your ID too. And what you don't got is any Iron Hand tattoos.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: I'll let you off this time, but don't let me catch you again.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Then can I get up now, officer?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: This is a blatant abuse of power. You can't treat me like this.
Her statement makes the patrol officer laugh out loud.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: 'Abuse of power'? Against you people? Hah! The only reason we're so busy these days is because we haven't been keeping you little shits in line.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Go ahead, make a report at the station. See if anyone cares what someone like you says.
The officer puts away his knife, but keeps his hand firmly planted on Hadiya's shoulder, preventing her from getting up.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Count yourself lucky you had all your paperwork on you today.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Otherwise I'd be hauling you back to the station for an interrogation.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Now pick up your toys and get out of here. Don't go swinging them around at night.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: And stay where you belong, you got that?
The officer tugs on Hadiya's clothes, intending to pull her up, but she brushes him aside.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: ...Don't touch me. I'm going.
She stands up on her own and picks up her swords, now soaked in rainwater.

steps.name: Columbian Patrol Officer
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Baba, was I...

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Wrong?
The rain has ceased. She looks towards the night sky hanging above her home, suddenly lost in thought.
Hadiya sits quietly on her bed, looking at the painting of the wilds hung up on her wall. It was a graduation present from her family, and apparently painted in authentic Sargonian style.
It used to just hang there, silently, with no significance except as a memento. But now, she feels like it is trying to tell her something.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: (Maybe I still have a choice.)
You there, Hadiya?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Salma?

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: Thank goodness you're alright!

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: Auntie Tarama told me what you told her at dinner.

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: They've gone too far, pushing you around like that!

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: It's fine, habibti. I'm not hurt.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: And now I know how you must've felt back then.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I was so naive, thinking you just happened to meet people who didn't like you.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: I never thought I'd run into the same thing.

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: What matters is that you're safe. An encounter like that could've gone a whole lot worse.

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: I don't even want to imagine what all our aunts and uncles would do if something actually happened to you.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Yeah yeah, but it didn't, so stop worrying about it.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: More importantly, I need to think about what to do next.

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: How about stick to within the neighborhood? They'll never give you a chance out there.

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: There's no shame in helping Auntie Tarama out. And it'll be safe too. Safe and happy.

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: Our aunts and uncles would be able to relax, too.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Spending the rest of my life here...

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: A lot of our older peers have already come back, haven't they?

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: It may not be a glamorous life, but it sure beats getting dirty looks wherever you go.

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: We've even had our candidates running in district elections.

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: We can run this place without having to rely on outsiders, and we won't have to go out and deal with discrimination either.

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: Just stay here. There's nothing wrong with life on 57th.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Sorry, Salma, but I just had a thought.
As she speaks, she looks towards her sneakers by the door, still soaked from the rain.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: You once said this is the only place in all the land that would always have my back.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: But I can't live my entire life here. I was always going to leave one day.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: So if I'd need to bust my butt to earn my place anywhere else anyway...

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Then why try in Sargon? At the very least, I can start fresh there.

steps.name: Salma
steps.text: Are... Are you serious, Hadiya?

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: If you asked me yesterday, I might have hesitated. But this time, I'm serious.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Compared to life in urban Columbia, I didn't know a thing about the wilderness. That was the biggest thing holding me back.
She reaches out, stroking the painting. She can almost hear the desert it depicts, and a voice calling out her name.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: But now, I understand.

steps.name: Hadiya
steps.text: Time to go see what a real wilderness is like.
